newsitem.title: USA: Boston pushes Pilgrim nuke restart to Sat.
newsitem.headline: Boston pushes Pilgrim nuke restart to Sat.

text.p: Boston Edison Co said Tuesday it pushed the restart of its 670 megawatt Pilgrim nuclear power plant in Plymouth, Mass., to this weekend after being shut a week ago for repairs.

"We're looking at a delay now to Saturday," said company spokesman Dave Tarantino, adding plant engineers needed more time to inspect the unit. The nuclear station was expected to resume operation Wednesday.
The Pilgrim station was taken off line last week due to saltwater intrusion in one of two sets of heat exchangers in its reactor building.
The utility decided it needed to examine the metal plates that provide support for both set of exchangers. The task would require the disassembly of the plates, he said.
The Pilgrim plant accounts for about one third of the Boston Edison's generating capacity.
